paper.title: SKILLFOUNDRY: Building Self-Evolving Agent Skill Libraries from Heterogeneous Scientific Resources
paper.central_claim: SkillFoundry, a tree-guided closed loop that mines heterogeneous scientific resources into executable, tested skill packages and expands/repairs/merges/prunes the library, yields a substantially novel (71.1% differing from SkillHub/SkillSMP) and internally valid 286-skill library whose skills improve a coding agent on five of six MoSciBench datasets, and can design on-demand task-specific skills that improve cell type annotation and the scDRS workflow.

gap.author_gap: Scientific procedural knowledge exists in heterogeneous resources but agents cannot operationalize it; existing skills are hand-crafted, narrow and limited-evaluated; tool-ecosystem work is tool-centric.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete direction (resource-to-skill conversion) is plausible and the scDRS case shows a concrete failure (agent omits filter-data) that a skill fixes; but the bottleneck is asserted rather than quantified (no analysis of how often missing procedural knowledge causes baseline failures) and existing skill libraries are only used for a novelty count, not as a performance baseline.
gap.lineage: Voyager skill library -> Anthropic skill packages -> failure-driven skill discovery (EvoSkill) / RL skill reuse / engineered skill bases; parallel line: ToolUniverse, Deploy-Master, Paper2Agent, ToolRosetta (tool conversion).
gap.closest_adjacent: Paper2Agent/ToolRosetta (resource-to-tool conversion) and EvoSkill/skill-mining work; the paper distinguishes by 'skill-centric' and 'heterogeneous resources' but gives no head-to-head.
gap.residue: Reliable conversion and maintenance of scientific procedural knowledge at scale.
gap.stakes: Silent scientific errors from misused tools (cited).
gap.method_response: Operational-contract extraction, multi-layer testing, tree-guided coverage, novelty/merge/prune.
gap.remaining_gap: Evidence that the tree-guided loop (vs plain mining or existing libraries) matters; utility-based retention evidence; breadth.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbor papers (EvoSkill, Paper2Agent, ToolRosetta, SkillHub/SkillSMP contents) are not in the pinned inputs; closest-adjacent comparison cannot be verified here and is requested in batch notes.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats retained; kept. A pre-built, retained library is toggled on later, external MoSciBench tasks with the agent fixed. This is weak, small-n evidence with no overlap audit, and on-demand skills are built for the evaluated task.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A 286-skill library that passes its own execution/synthetic tests is associated with +5 (Repo) / +8 (Paper) of ~88 MoSciBench items for one coding agent in a single run (four or five of six datasets, depending on scorer). Two on-demand skills improve one cell-annotation run and a three-replicate scDRS comparison. Novelty is keyword-judged, and the self-evolving loop's contribution is not isolated.
unresolved: Which skills were made available per MoSciBench dataset, and by whom.
Design-case vs evaluation separation for on-demand skills.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Fragmented resources → usable skills is a real limitation with named tool- and skill-centric neighbours (son55:E018, E019). The bottleneck is asserted, and existing libraries are not used as a comparator.

M.reason: Opus → son55 2 (sol 3). Tree-guided mining → contract → multi-layer tests → merge/prune is a coherent response (son55:E002, sol:E09). But the retention signals measure executability, mock-input stability and keyword novelty, not usefulness (son55:E003). The layer-2 'skill vs no-skill' utility check has no reported cases or outcomes (son55:E021), and the authors concede internal validation is only screening (son55:E006). There is no distinguishing prediction against handing the agent the raw documentation. Key assumptions are thin → 2.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Stages, model allocation, registry states and controlled state mutation are described (son55:E022, E023). Missing: layer-2 thresholds, rollback, conflict handling, and how 'the relevant' skills reach the agent at use time (son55:E026).

E.measurement.reason: Opus → son55 2 (sol 3). Downstream metrics are partly credible: the official and paper MoSciBench scorers, and blinded expert scDRS grading with RMSE (son55:E015, sol:E07). But two of the paper's three headline claims rest on self-judged measurements: 'internally valid' means passing its own tests, with unreported failure counts (opus:O04), and 71.1% novelty is a keyword search (son55:E005). The 'five of six' summary also misstates the official-scorer result (four of six; opus:O02, O03).

E.causality.reason: Opus → son55 1 (sol 2). The only manipulation is skills present vs absent for a fixed agent (son55:E026). Unlike a starter-vs-evolved design, the no-skill arm also lacks all domain documentation, so pipeline value cannot be separated from 'any relevant guidance'. There is no SkillHub/SkillSMP, raw-doc or RAG control, and no ablation of tree guidance, validation layers, repair or novelty pruning. The cell-annotation comparison pits a task-built skill against vanilla Codex, with SpatialAgent still better (son55:E012). Relevant but not attributable → 1.

E.holdout.reason: Opus → son55 2 (sol 1). MoSciBench is an external benchmark evaluated with an already-mined library, and nothing says it was used in construction (son55:E024). There is no overlap audit, though mining draws on papers/repos MoSciBench may derive from. The skills used are 'the relevant' ones, selector unstated (son55:E026).
